title: U.S. House · Ohio's 2nd District
area: Southwestern Ohio, including parts of the Cincinnati suburbs and southeastern Ohio counties

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 2nd District R+21, one of the more strongly Republican-leaning seats in Ohio's 2026 map.

candidates.name: David Taylor
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent; defeated Bob Carr in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary, 75.0% to 25.0%

positions.summary: His official site says he will continue to stand for pro-life policies and laws that defend the lives of unborn children.
positions.quote: I will continue to stand for pro-life policies and laws that defend the lives of unborn children.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management and Credit) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials; Water Resources and Environment) in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Jen Mazzuckelli
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, 53.3% to 46.7%, over Todd Wilson

priorities.text: Says Congress needs a representative who 'genuinely listens to our concerns and is responsive to OUR needs' and 'acts as a public servant NOT a politician,' criticizing incumbent David Taylor for refusing in-person town halls.
priorities.quote: We need a representative who genuinely listens to our concerns and is responsive to OUR needs. We need a representative that acts as a public servant NOT a politician.

priorities.text: Says a key responsibility of Congress is oversight of the executive branch, including scrutinizing spending and released frozen or impounded appropriations.

statements.quote: We need a representative who fulfills their basic Constitutional responsibilities - the power of the purse, and the power to declare war.
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, 2026

candidates.researchNotes: From her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026) and campaign website. Her site (Jen4OH2.com) has an about page but no issue pages. Her war-powers remark is shown as a statement because it does not say whether Congress should approve each military action.
